patch.value: Recurring reminders: a standing check (daily release-health, weekly governance sweep) re-arms itself on fire instead of requiring manual re-scheduling

Reminders are single-fire (at=...,text=... only); events already expand recurrence (pm-vg5h) but reminders do not. A standing operational check such as pm-7zs0 (daily auto-release verification) must be re-scheduled by hand after every fire, which means the safety net silently disappears the first time the re-schedule is forgotten. Add an opt-in recurrence field to the reminder facet (cadence + next-fire derivation, re-arm recorded as a history mutation), consistent with the calendar recurrence model and the builtin-calendar package boundary (pm-o3fh). Horizon: near-mid; small surface, high operational value.

value.text:
Direct evidence 2026-07-30 (evening): the interim manual cadence failed exactly the way this item predicts, and it failed silently.

The release-health reminder carried one armed entry, at 2026-07-27T06:00Z, whose own text ended with the instruction to re-schedule the next daily reminder. It fired on the 27th and was never re-armed. For three days the reminder that exists to verify the daily release published nothing, signalled nothing, and appeared in no surface as overdue or missing. The item itself stayed open the whole time, so nothing about its status distinguished an armed recurring check from a dead one. I re-armed it by hand for 2026-07-31 during this pass, which restores the signal and also demonstrates that the workaround requires a human or an agent to notice the absence of a signal in order to restore it.

That is the sharpest argument for this feature. A recurring check whose continuation depends on someone reading the fired reminder's own text is not a recurring check, it is a one-shot with an instruction attached. The failure mode is silence rather than error, so the interval between lapse and discovery is bounded only by how often someone happens to inspect the item.

Two mechanical notes for the implementation. --clear-reminders cannot be combined with --reminder in one call, so re-arming today takes two mutations and is briefly in a state with no reminder at all, which a crash between the two would make permanent. And the arming record is replaced rather than appended, so there is no history in the item of how many times a recurring reminder has fired. If re-arming becomes automatic, the fire count and the last fire time are worth keeping on the item, because they are the only evidence that the recurrence is alive.
